name: Canary Islands, Spain

visa.notes: Non-lucrative visa requires proof of sufficient funds (~€2,400/mo). Cannot work in Spain on this visa.

rent.notes: idealista Oct 2026: Canarias EUR 15.2/m2 (+4.5% y/y), Santa Cruz de Tenerife province EUR 15.3; Las Palmas de Gran Canaria city EUR 14.0 and Santa Cruz city EUR 13.3 at end-2025. An 85-95 m2 pet-friendly 2-3BR = EUR 1,200-1,450 in the capitals; tourist-south municipalities (Adeje, Arona, San Bartolome) run EUR 19-22/m2. Numbeo LPGC Nov 2026: 3BR EUR 1,146 outside centre, EUR 1,370 centre; Barometro del Alquiler Q1 2026 average rent EUR 1,135.

groceries.notes: OCU 2026 study: average household basket EUR 6,602/yr (EUR 550/mo) nationally; Las Palmas shows a wide price spread (EUR 2,167/yr savings potential) and island import costs offset the lower IGIC. Food CPI +2.3% y/y Aug 2026. Includes about EUR 60-80/mo of food for a 100 lb dog.

utilities.notes: Mild climate, no heating: electricity about EUR 85-100 (PVPC average bill EUR 88/mo at 3,500 kWh/yr, Oct 2026), butane EUR 15 per cylinder for cooking/hot water, desalinated water plus sewer about EUR 30. Numbeo LPGC basic utilities EUR 101 (70-200). Excludes internet.

healthcare.notes: Resident retiree couple age 60 on private full-cover policies (required for the non-lucrative visa; pre-existing conditions can be loaded or excluded). Poliza Medica Nov 2026 market average at age 60: EUR 91/person full cover with copays, EUR 123/person no-copay; Sanitas Mas Salud 60-64 no-copay EUR 186 (Valencia) to EUR 220 (Barcelona) per person. Typical = 2 x EUR 123; after 1 year of legal residency the public SNS becomes an option via the convenio especial (not priced here). No Canarias-specific insurer quote found; max uses the Barcelona Sanitas quote as an upper bound.

insurance.notes: Renters/contents (seguro de inquilino) policy only: Selectra quotes EUR 70-300/yr (Tuio 79, Caser 110, Santalucia 141 for a 71 m2 flat); full owner-type home policies average about EUR 265/yr nationally (Selectra 2026 report), used as the upper bound. Typical about EUR 140/yr. Re-modeled from old template (stored 125 was health cover). Las Palmas EUR 267/yr and Santa Cruz EUR 258/yr average home premiums.

petCare.notes: Large dog, no food: annual vaccines incl. rabies EUR 50-80, 2 consults EUR 30-60 each, monthly antiparasitic pipette EUR 8-15 plus quarterly worming EUR 12-20, periodic dental cleaning EUR 100-250 (cuantomecuesta, Apr 2026); giant-breed dosing and Bernese health risks push the typical above the EUR 200-400/yr healthy-pet estimate. Island vet prices track the mainland; fewer specialists, so referrals may mean travel.

petDaycare.notes: Occasional use: about 6-8 daycare days per month at the Cronoshare national average EUR 16/day (range 9-30) plus one week of boarding per year; residencias caninas exist on Gran Canaria and Tenerife (Valsequillo, Granadilla).

petGrooming.notes: Giant long/double coat: bath EUR 42-47, brush-out EUR 20-24, tidy-up EUR 46-51 per visit (Cronoshare 2026 national price guide); modeled as one full groom per month with a brush-out in between.

sources.title: Cronoshare: cuanto cuesta peluqueria canina (precios 2026)

transportation.notes: Guaguas and tram are free for recurring (bono) travelers across Canarias through 2026 (state aid renewed Dec 2025), so transit costs little. A car: insurance EUR 394/yr (CHECK24), gasolina about EUR 1.32/l in Las Palmas (Mar 2026; no mainland hydrocarbon tax) for 800 km/mo = EUR 75, maintenance/ITV/IVTM about EUR 45. Island living usually needs a car.

Stored value included a US Google Fi line; add roughly EUR 45/mo if that line is kept.

healthcare.system: Spanish SCS (Servicio Canario de Salud) with good hospitals in major cities. Air evacuation to mainland for complex cases.
healthcare.waitTimes: Public: 3-10 weeks for specialists. Private options more limited than mainland.
healthcare.prescriptionCoverage: Standard Spanish prescription coverage with co-pays

pros: Year-round warm and mild climate (eternal spring)

pros.text: Lower IGIC general rate (7%) instead of mainland IVA (21%) under the Canary Islands Special Tax Regime

cons.text: Island isolation - flights to mainland are 2.5+ hours
Limited shopping and cultural options vs mainland
Some goods more expensive due to shipping costs
Safety & crime: see cited reports for current figures by city and country
